subject: art-design
title: Annotation & Analysis: Stretch
welcome_lead: Add critical vocabulary, cross-reference artists and weigh competing readings.
meta_desc: Stretch GCSE analysis: comparative analysis, art criticism vocabulary, multiple readings.
final_note: Top marks come from comparison, not just description.

concepts.def: Examining two works side by side for similarity.
Study of symbols and what they mean.
Suggested or cultural meaning of a symbol.
Literal, surface meaning of a symbol.
Detailed evaluation, often using set criteria.

walkthroughs.body_html: Put two artists side by side: same subject, different methods. Compare composition, media, palette, intention. Then explain what each artist gains by their choice. This shows examiners you can think structurally, not just list facts.

A skull denotes a human bone, but in 17th-century Vanitas painting it connotes mortality and the shortness of life. Strong analysis explains both layers and links them to the work's iconography and context.

Sophisticated critique allows that a work can mean different things to different viewers. Use phrases like "one reading is…", "alternatively…", "in its time it was seen as…". Acknowledge limits in your evidence rather than overclaiming.
